notes:
- iPhone ProRAW photos open at the exposure the phone gave them, where bright scenes used to open up to two stops over and dark ones up to four stops under. Brightness and color can still differ a little from the phone's own preview.
- Pixel and Samsung Expert RAW files follow the instructions their own files carry in the same way, and Samsung thumbnails use the phone's own preview.
- Phone photos saved before this update catch up when opened, batch exported or baked, unless you had changed their Tone Profile.
- Finish adjustment layers (Exposure, Curves, Levels, White Balance, Color, Color Balance, Black & White) correct the picture at its true brightness, as the same controls do in Develop. Existing ones keep their numbers and look different.
- Adjustments inside a Finish group read the layers below them, clipped adjustments change only the layer they are clipped to, and grouping keeps a layer's blend mode and clipping.
- Layer effects keep their size between Fit and the export, reach past a placed picture's edge, and are written into an exported layer. Large shadows render much faster.
- Finish adjustments and layer effects have their full controls on their Graph nodes.
- Depth Lighting: a directional light has Elevation, Depth and Reach sliders, so it can land on the background or light every plane alike. Existing lights look the same.
- Adjustment layers have the Export box on their sections: the picture as a section leaves it on that layer writes into a TIFF or EXR export as a layer of its own.
- A layer added after a section's Export box was ticked always lands on the picture; it could end up on the export's branch and change nothing.
- The Export panel's progress line names the file being written, with the extension of the format you chose.
- The line Thickness slider has its full width wherever it appears, and its number drags sideways.
- The Develop panel holds still while you drag a Depth Map slider with Recolor open.
- A script that is still sending when the scripting API refuses its request now reads the refusal; the connection could reset first.
